fields.value: Fail over across providers, regions and GPUs when renting

## Problem

On 2026-11-17 RunPod, Vast and Lium all had no rentable GPU for most of a morning; a measurement approved at USD 3 took four rentals and still had no number. Each Etude on-demand is tied to one provider and one GPU, so a refusal only retries the same source. Task 943fa5 (PR #125) adds EC2 and Lambda and spot, but a person still has to notice a refusal and pick another on-demand by hand. SkyPilot's core feature is the opposite: an ordered or any-of list of candidate resources, with automatic failover across zones, regions and clouds.

## Outcome

One named thing a person rents from can list candidates, for example "L4 or A10 or 4090, on RunPod, then Vast, then EC2, then Lambda, cheapest first", spot or standard price, and:

- `etude availability NAME` shows each candidate's answer (price, or the refusal: quota, no spot, no stock, unknown GPU, missing key) and which one would be rented.
- `etude rent` / `launch --rent` try candidates in order (or by price) after a definite refusal, without a person stepping in.
- The run's dollar cap, hours, machine timer and launcher cleanup hold across whichever provider wins; a run resumed after a lost machine may land on a different provider.

## Constraints

- Builds on PR #125 (EC2, Lambda, spot, per-zone EC2 spot fallback) and should agree with Task 2daf03 (one rental lifecycle; renaming "on-demand"). Settle the order with 2daf03 before building.
- Each candidate's quote must stay a live provider price; the cap is checked against the candidate actually rented.
- Refusal reasons stay distinct per candidate so `availability` explains why each was passed over.
- SkyPilot comparison research (/Users/jack/src/etude/scratch/skypilot-comparison-2026-11-17.md (Codex research, SkyPilot at 844eb673)) is prior art to read first.
